trace=[
  {"step":1,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"fuzz_parse_http_request","line":1669,"var":"request.flags","code":".flags = REQUEST_ALLOW_PROXY_REQS","note":"The fuzz harness enables PROXY protocol parsing for attacker-controlled input, so the first bytes of the buffer are interpreted as a PROXY header before HTTP parsing.","depends_on":[]},
  {"step":2,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_http_request","line":1195,"var":"buffer","code":"buffer = parse_proxy_protocol(request, buffer);","note":"The request buffer is handed to the PROXY parser when the flag is set, making the raw input the source of the vulnerable path.","depends_on":[{"on":1,"type":"data","via":"request flag"}]},
  {"step":3,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol","line":1179,"var":"buffer[0..3]","code":"case MULTICHAR_CONSTANT('P','R','O','X'): return parse_proxy_protocol_v1(request, buffer);","note":"Inputs beginning with PROXY dispatch into the v1 parser, which assumes a fixed-format header and then tokenizes it in place.","depends_on":[{"on":2,"type":"data","via":"buffer prefix"}]},
  {"step":4,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol_v1","line":170,"var":"protocol","code":"protocol = buffer + sizeof(\"PROXY \") - 1;","note":"The parser advances past the literal prefix and treats the remainder of the attacker-controlled line as the protocol/address fields.","depends_on":[{"on":3,"type":"data","via":"buffer contents"}]},
  {"step":5,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"strsep_char","line":148,"var":"ptr","code":"ptr = strchr(strp, delim);","note":"Each field split searches for the next space inside the same mutable buffer; malformed or short fields can leave later pointers NULL while earlier delimiters are still overwritten.","depends_on":[{"on":4,"type":"data","via":"protocol string"}]},
  {"step":6,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol_v1","line":171,"var":"src_addr","code":"src_addr = strsep_char(protocol, ' ');","note":"The first split writes a NUL terminator into the buffer and returns the next field pointer, so subsequent parsing depends on the exact spacing supplied by the attacker.","depends_on":[{"on":5,"type":"data","via":"delimiter search"}]},
  {"step":7,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol_v1","line":172,"var":"dst_addr","code":"dst_addr = strsep_char(src_addr, ' ');","note":"The second split continues walking the same buffer; if the header is truncated or space-separated fields are missing, later dereferences operate on invalid assumptions.","depends_on":[{"on":6,"type":"data","via":"in-place tokenization"}]},
  {"step":8,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol_v1","line":173,"var":"src_port","code":"src_port = strsep_char(dst_addr, ' ');","note":"The third split produces the source-port token that is later consumed by numeric parsing, keeping the attacker-controlled pointer chain alive.","depends_on":[{"on":7,"type":"data","via":"in-place tokenization"}]},
  {"step":9,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol_v1","line":174,"var":"dst_port","code":"dst_port = strsep_char(src_port, ' ');","note":"The fourth split is the last field extraction before validation; the parser now relies on the presence of a CRLF-terminated line with all tokens present.","depends_on":[{"on":8,"type":"data","via":"in-place tokenization"}]},
  {"step":10,"file":"src/lib/lwan-request.c","function":"parse_proxy_protocol_v1","line":164,"var":"end[1]","code":"end = memchr(buffer, '\\r', line_size); if (!end || end[1] != '\\n') return NULL;","note":"The root cause is a fixed-size scan over 108 bytes of attacker-controlled input; if the CR is found at the end of the accessible buffer, the unconditional read of end[1] can go one byte past the mapped input and trigger the ASan global-buffer-overflow read.","depends_on":[{"on":4,"type":"data","via":"buffer length and terminator placement"}]}]
p.write_text(__import__('json').dumps(trace, indent=2))
print(p.read_text())
